static_traits.name: Lin Shan
static_traits.family_status: Father was a chef, later became a bartender
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive spouse to confide in, but topics about cooking and family expectations are rather sensitive
static_traits.medical_history: Never received psychotherapy, no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Markedly negative expression, self-reproach, frequent use of 'should' phrasing and comparison; high emotional tension; good cooperativeness

basic_info.main_problem: I have developed a strong aversion to cooking; because Father is a chef I feel I 'should' excel at this skill, which makes me feel guilty and not good enough. These feelings started in adolescence and became more prominent after marrying and having children. Whenever I compare with Father's cooking, or at family gatherings and when cooking for my children, this pressure and negative emotion markedly intensifies. I tried taking cooking classes to improve my skills, but the pressure and negative feelings remain.
basic_info.core_demands: Hoping to address the emotional burden and self-critical thoughts related to cooking skills and Father's career expectations.
growth_experiences: In the family of origin, Father was seen as the benchmark of being 'good at cooking' as a chef; the client began internalizing Father's standards as self-demands in adolescence, forming the value condition of 'I should be good at cooking'. After marrying and having children, family roles and caregiving demands increased, and family and friends' expectations of her cooking rose; the client frequently compared her own ability with Father's at family gatherings and when cooking for her children, gradually accumulating guilt, shame, and not-good-enough experiences, reinforcing cooking-related pressure and Self-denial.

core_beliefs: My worth depends on whether I meet the family's (father's) expectations
I am not good enough (a failure), especially at cooking

special_situations.event: Being expected to cook at family gatherings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot cook as well as Father, I will disappoint my family, proving I am not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Preparing extensively in advance, enrolling in cooking classes to make up for inadequacy, or avoiding complex dishes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will mess it up; I disappointed my family; I am inferior to Father

special_situations.event: Disagrees with spouse over sharing cooking duties
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the food is not good, I am an incompetent wife and mother
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Argues with the spouse or reduces cooking, instead taking on other housework to prove value
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am a failure as a wife and mother

special_situations.event: When preparing dinner alone for the children
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot reach Father's level, it shows I have no ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly practicing, consulting recipes, taking cooking classes to improve skills
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never be as good as Dad

special_situations.event: When planning a week's menu for the family, thinks 'I must cook the food well'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I must be a good chef, because Father is a chef
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forcing oneself to invest in practice, urging improvement through self-harshness
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should be able to do it; otherwise it is failure

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized and affirmed, to be seen as valuable and good enough as a daughter, wife, and mother
core_conflict.fear: Fearing failure and being dismissed, worrying about disappointing family and being seen as incompetent
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being criticized and feeling shame by catering to expectations (improving cooking skills) or avoiding (cooking less, turning to other housework)
Maintains a sense of control over self-improvement through self-reproach

object_relations.self_representation: Inferior to Father, a daughter prone to failure

object_relations.object_representation: A demanding spouse with clear expectations

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor explores the self-worth standards related to the father's occupation or points out their 'should' beliefs
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client subconsciously sees the counselor as a demanding and judging other, feeling scrutinized and not good enough (transference: projecting external expectations onto the current relationship)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a gentle, supportive tone, naming the 'internalization' pattern, inviting her to distinguish 'family expectations' from 'self choice', guiding her with empathetic questioning to express needs and boundaries in her own language, avoiding critical or confrontational inquiry.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing her unmet expectations or comparing Father's ability triggers intense shame
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Turning outward anger and dissatisfaction against the self, believing I am a failure who deserves blame (self-attack)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Inviting her to notice self-critical language in an accepting, warm tone, using restructuring and self-compassion exercises, emphasizing concrete observable efforts and strengths, reducing absolutist evaluations.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked about the specific evidence for and alternative explanations of cooking pressure
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Avoids contacting painful feelings by providing logical reasons to explain the belief that 'I must cook well'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: While affirming their thinking ability, guides them back to present experience (bodily sensations, emotion vocabulary), carrying emotions with short sentences and a slow pace, reducing abstraction.

manifestations: Bound by family and father's standards, internalizing the value condition 'should be good at cooking'
In the division of housework, lacking a sense of choice, feeling one must meet the standard
Frequently compares with the father's level, weakening her own uniqueness and preferences

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using 'I should' and 'I must' when talking about cooking
Takes his father's cooking standards as his own absolute requirements
Takes family expectations as the core basis of self-evaluation

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Turns resentment about family expectations into self-harshness and self-deprecation
Not expressing needs in stressful situations, turning to inner self-blame instead
Reduces cooking, turns to other housework for self-regulation

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Caring excessively about others' evaluations and expectations
In cooking-related situations, is cautious and careful, with marked stress

positive_force: Has transferable personal strengths (skilled at and loves sewing)
Proactively tries to improve (taking cooking classes)
Work performance stable (bartender work not affected)
negative_force: Internalizing family expectations and Father's standards, forming rigid 'should' rules
Excessive comparison and Self-denial, labeling as 'failure'
Closely binds self-worth to family role performance (cooking)
Intense anxiety and shame triggered in family gathering and cooking-for-children situations
Conflicts with spouse over cooking division leading to relationship tension

target_behavior.behavior: Strong anxiety and self-criticism when facing cooking tasks, accompanied by avoidance or over-preparation
antecedent: Being expected to cook at family gatherings
Thinking about needing to plan the week's menu
target_behavior.core_reason: Internalizes the father's cooking standards as self-worth rules, compares and catastrophizes the consequences of failure, using 'should' statements to drive self-reproach
target_behavior.function: Avoids being judged and shame, maintains a sense of control over self-improvement
target_behavior.consequence: Daily life affected (decreased meal planning and enjoyment), rising emotional tension, persistent guilt and Self-denial

target_behavior.behavior: Arguing with spouse over cooking responsibilities
antecedent: Spouse discussing or asking to share cooking
Being told or hinted that cooking is not up to standard
target_behavior.core_reason: Self-worth and family role are threatened, triggering defensiveness (labeling as 'failure' and black-and-white evaluations)
target_behavior.function: Defending self-esteem, displacing pressure and external conflict
target_behavior.consequence: Partner relationship tension, declining communication quality, further aggravating cooking-related pressure
